description: Full profile of one surf town: description, season, water temperature, wave types, levels and curated surf spots (each with its type, level, the way its coast faces in degrees (facing), its best tide where known (tide, e.g. "low to mid, rising", with tideSources), reviewed, freely licensed photos of surf at that break when there are any (photo: the first; photos: up to 5, someone surfing first, each with author and licence: credit them), and reviewed YouTube surf clips filmed there: clips[].url). `dataQuality` says how far to trust the town's data (trust 0–100 and level high/medium/low, when it was last checked against sources, how many spots are verified, open audit warnings): tell the user when trust is low or the data was never checked. `surfByMonth` gives, for each month, how often the surf was good there, measured over the last three years (goodDays, greatDays: % of days rated Good or better / Great or better at the best spot; seaTempC: the mean sea temperature measured by satellite, NASA JPL MUR SST; waveHeightM; rainMm: the mean rain of the month in town) and drySeason (the measured dry months, or all/none), with its source: use it for "when should I go" (the waves, and the weather for the trip) and say it is measured, not a forecast. `seasons` answers "is it worth going outside the season, and what should I expect": season (the best months with their measured good/great days, wave height, sea and rain), allYear, and rest: the other months in runs (Biarritz: summer and winter), each compared with the season (waves smaller/bigger/same, water warmer/colder, rain wetter/drier, surf worth/fewer/rare), forLearners (smaller waves at a town with beginner spots), nearlyAsGood (a month in the run nearly as good as the season: a shoulder month) and inSeasonNearby (towns within 300 km whose own season it is then, e.g. Keramas on Bali's east coast when the Bukit's season is over).
name: get_town
title: Get a surf town
